newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open little changed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open little changed in quiet trade.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened little changed in very quiet trade on Friday, with the lack of a U.S. market or significant Canadian economic data keeping activity muted, analysts said.

"Dead is the best word," said one bond dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "With the U.S. closed there's a little bit of activity, but it's pretty quiet and I don't expect it to change throughout the day. There's no catalyst. Nothing to move it."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.17 to C$117.05 to yield 6.675 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond last traded with a yield of 6.62 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to six basis points from seven basis points at Thursday's close.
Canadian bond market activity was light with U.S. markets closed for Independence Day. Analysts said volumes were expected to decline even further in the afteroon.
But there was no official recommendation of an early close from the Toronto Bond Traders' Association.
"There has beens some discussion about (closing at) 2 o'clock, but so far nothing official has come out," the dealer said.
In economic news, Statistics Canada reported that labor income rose 0.5 percent in April to C$37.084 billion from C$36.889 billion in March.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.14 to C$108.54 to yield 6.087 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent, which last traded to yield 6.30 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 21 basis points from 19 basis points at the close of trading on Thursday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.06 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.15 percent.
